title: LayoutDSL
description: Public schema for Layout DSL v1.0 (ADR-045, ADR-055). This is the SHAPE contract: it fixes the closed set of fields and the enum vocabularies. Cross-reference resolution, ref uniqueness, and other MEANING checks stay in LayoutValidator.js (ADR-064 Phase 2). additionalProperties:false makes an unknown field a rejection, mirroring the grasp-contract discipline (PHILOSOPHY #29).

version.description: Layout DSL version. Bound to LAYOUT_DSL_VERSION by the drift test.

strategy.description: Placement strategy for unpositioned entities. Bound to VALID_STRATEGIES.

axis.description: Axis token for linear/radial strategies. Bound to VALID_AXES.

type.description: Entity type expressible in Layout DSL. Bound to VALID_ENTITY_TYPES.

parentRef.description: For a standalone CoordinateFrame, the ref of another entity it is a TF child of (e.g. tcp → robot_base). When present, `position`/`rotation` are the LOCAL offset from that parent; when absent, they are the world pose (world-parented root). Robot TF tree world → robot_base → tcp (ADR-084 §2 revised).

robotRole.description: Declared role of a CoordinateFrame inside a robot's TF tree (ADR-090): 'base' = world-parented root (where the arm stands), 'tcp' = its tool-point child. This is what makes a robot identifiable as an ENTITY rather than by the magic name `robot_base`, so a scene can carry N robots. Absent = an ordinary frame belonging to no robot.

mountedOn.description: ADR-151: what a robot tcp's `position`/`rotation` are measured from. 'flange' = they ARE the tool mount (tool0 -> tcp) — the end effector's own fact and the interface the robot and its end effector share; the world pose is derived (base ∘ flange-at-rest ∘ mount), never stored. Absent on a pre-ADR-151 tcp, whose base-relative value the importer replaces with the default mount and announces (the entity and every relation to it survive).

hand.description: ADR-152 D3: WHAT a robot grasps with — only on a robot tcp (`robotRole: tcp`, `mountedOn: flange`), the interface the robot and its end effector share. The hand's kind, its grasp-gate parameters and, optionally, its SHAPE (a housing + two fingers, or a housing + a cup), in the Layout length unit (mm) in the FLANGE frame (+Z out of the flange face, jaws closing along ±X). The wire `gripper`, the arm's drawn tool and the hand preview are all derived from this one declaration. Absent = the hand is UNDECLARED (never filled in with a default on read). The shape is optional; when declared it must agree with the tool mount (jaw: body length ≤ mount ≤ body + finger length; cup: mount = body length + cupHeight) or the search stops with the reason. Structural validity per kind (body+fingers / body+cupHeight together) is checked by the front's resolver, which reports a malformed hand rather than dropping it.

maxOpening.description: Jaw: maximum opening (mm). The fingers are drawn and judged OPEN at this width.

fingerClearance.description: Jaw: extra clearance the fingers need beside the part (mm).

body.description: The housing from the flange face to the palm: a cylinder (radius, length) or a box (size [x, y, z], z = length).

fingers.description: Jaw: one finger — thickness along X, width along Y, length along Z from the palm (mm).

cupHeight.description: Cup: height below the housing along the flange +Z (mm). The cup face is the TCP.

innerDimensions.description: Inner (cavity) full extents of a HOLLOW body such as a tray, bin or tote (ADR-133 D1). Wall and floor thicknesses are DERIVED from this and `dimensions` -- (outer-inner)/2 per horizontal axis, outer.z-inner.z for the floor -- rather than declared, so the two cannot disagree (§1.1). Absent means the body is solid; it is never defaulted to zero, which would make "no cavity declared" and "a cavity of zero size" the same value (原則 #31). The cavity is open at the top: a lid is a separate body.

graspFeature.description: Declares HOW a Solid should be grasped (ADR-119 D2 / ADR-128 / ADR-152 D1). OPTIONAL: with no graspFeature the front derives the faces from the declared hand (ADR-118) and the panel says so — absence is a state ("nobody said"), distinct from an explicit `anywhere` ("I looked and chose not to narrow"). A closed kind-discriminated union, same governance as `gripper` (ADR-118): the kind decides which fields exist. Declared specs are used VERBATIM and never merged with the derived set (ADR-119 D3) unless the strategy itself declares `fallback: derived`.

kind.description: `anywhere` = declared and deliberately not narrowed (samples follow the hand's derived faces). `specs` = grasp only as the listed grasp specs say, used as `strategy` says. `faces` is the pre-ADR-152 face list: still READ and migrated to specs on load (each face → one spec approaching from it, strategy `score`/`none` — the same answer), never written.

specs.description: Required when kind is `specs`: at least one grasp spec, in priority order.

faces.description: LEGACY (kind `faces`, pre-ADR-152): read and migrated to specs, never written. At least one face, each with an optional normalised region.

graspSpec.description: One named way to grasp this workpiece (ADR-152 D1) — a GRASP SPEC. Bundles the facts one 'face' could not hold: where the hand comes from (`approach.from` — the APPROACH face, whose outward normal the hand travels against), over which part of it (`approach.region`), how far it may tilt (`approach.tiltTolerance`), which LOCAL axis the jaws close on (`closing`; the two CONTACT faces are derived from it, never declared), and how deep the TCP goes below the approach face (`depth`, mm). The spec list's ORDER is its priority. Declaration only — whether the jaws close, whether the hand hits anything, which spec's candidates come back is solved in core/.

name.description: Unique within the list. Results are reported per spec by this name.

hand.description: Which hand this spec is written for. A spec the declared hand cannot use is not an error — it is excluded from the run with a reason; when every spec is excluded the run stops (it never falls back silently).

from.description: The APPROACH face, by its outward LOCAL axis (turns with the object).

tiltTolerance.description: Largest tilt (radians) from the face-on approach. Omitted = every declared sampling tilt.

closing.description: Jaws only: the LOCAL axis the jaws close along. Must not be the approach axis. Omitted = every roll is tried and the width is measured from the samples (the pre-ADR-152 behaviour).

depth.description: Jaws only: how far below the approach face the TCP goes, in the Layout length unit (mm). Omitted = 0, on the face.

graspStrategy.description: How this workpiece's specs are used (ADR-152 D1) — a GRASP STRATEGY. 0 or 1 per Solid. Omitted = `priority` / `none`, and the panel SAYS it was omitted (a default is not a choice the user made — 原則 #31).

order.description: priority: return only the candidates of the first spec (in list order) that has any. score: mix every spec's candidates by score.

fallback.description: none: no spec feasible → no candidate. derived: only then, search the faces the hand derives (ADR-118).

faceRegion.description: A sub-region of one face, NORMALISED to 0..1 across that face's two in-plane axes (u,v), so it means the same fraction whatever the solid's size — a region in metres would stop covering the face the day the box is resized. Omitted = the whole face. A grasp needs AREA, so this is a rectangle and never a single point (a jaw needs finger width, a cup needs its diameter).

jointType.description: URDF kinematic joint type, or null for a topological-only link. Bound to VALID_JOINT_TYPES.

semanticType.description: Domain semantic type. Bound to VALID_SEMANTIC_TYPES.

properties.description: Domain-open property bag (connector, distance_mm, voltage_V, note, ...). Kept open on purpose — property names are extensible.
